title: Risk Assessment: documenter agent snapshot-not-ledger + bounded documentation-corpus cleanup
summary: Technical risk assessment for #3288 as scoped by the operator and resolved HITL (cq-1 = enumerated targets + bounded sweep, defer long tail; cq-2 = no automated guardrail this round). Two coupled work streams: (1) a small, text-only revision of the documenter agent's task instructions (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py 'Your Task' assembly + shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py DOCUMENTER_ROLE) so it writes current-state snapshots and never leaks SDLC artifacts (slice-N/TASK-N/phase/HITL ids) into durable docs; (2) a bounded pass over the existing corpus (263 files carry ledger refs, grep-verified 2026-06-26) to strip ledger narration while preserving design rationale. Overall risk is LOW-MEDIUM. Work stream 1 is genuinely low risk (text edits, no behavior change) with two concrete test-preservation seams. The dominant risk lives in work stream 2 and is one of JUDGMENT and ROLE-ROUTING, not engineering: (a) the documenter's own gateway boundary BLOCKS code-file writes, so any docstring/inline-comment cleanup in *.py files cannot be done by the documenter and must be routed to coder or the cleanup will hit a gateway impasse; (b) over-zealous deletion can strip load-bearing rationale the issue explicitly says to keep; (c) with no automated guardrail (cq-2), the only durable anti-drift mechanism is the strength of the work-stream-1 prompt revision itself. Recommendation: PROCEED_WITH_MITIGATIONS.
scope_note: Grounded against the confirmed refine analysis (.egg-state/drafts/3288-analysis.md), the live issue task_description, both resolved HITL decisions (cq-1, cq-2), and the working tree on 2026-06-26. The task_planner plan artifact (3288-plan*.md/json) was not yet present on this branch when this assessment was drafted; risks are framed against the issue's two work streams and the real code touchpoints. Reconcile against the planner's slice DAG on review — see plan_reconciliation_pending.

risks.title: Prompt-revision string assertions in test_pipeline_prompts.py
risks.description: The work-stream-1 edit rewrites the documenter 'Your Task' text. Two existing assertions constrain the rewrite: test_documenter_phase_intro_text requires the substring 'Focus your documentation' to survive (currently from the 6761-6763 'Focus your documentation on changes from plan phase {id}' line), and test_documenter_prompt_includes_external_research requires the WebSearch/WebFetch external-research block (14796-14798) to remain. Note the 6763 line embeds `phase_obj.id` — a phase iteration number — but it lives in the PROMPT the agent reads, not in a durable doc the agent writes, so the issue's 'no SDLC artifacts in docs' rule does not strictly forbid it; still, rewording it to drop the chronological 'changes from plan phase {id}' framing better models the snapshot principle.
risks.mitigation: Coder must run orchestrator/tests/test_pipeline_prompts.py after the edit and update assertions in lockstep with intentional wording changes. If the 'Focus your documentation' phrase is reworded, update test_documenter_phase_intro_text; keep the external-research block (or update its test deliberately). Prefer ADDING a positive assertion that the new snapshot-principle instruction text is present, so the standard is regression-guarded (this is the only durable anti-drift guard given cq-2).

risks.title: BRC no-op / no-doc-impact propose path regression
risks.description: The issue and CLAUDE directive REQUIRE preserving the no-op propose path (the '### When the slice warrants no doc updates (#3027)' block at 14800-14826 and the plan-phase variant ~14157). A cleanup pass that touches this block to scrub its 'e.g. slice-3 is a pure decomposition' example string (14817) could accidentally alter the `--no-changes-needed --no-changes-reason` mechanics or delete the block's instruction to still propose, which would silently break BRC convergence (a documenter that heartbeats without proposing blocks consensus indefinitely).
risks.mitigation: Treat the no-op block as behavior-bearing, not prose: limit any edit to the EXAMPLE reason string (reword 'slice-3 ...' to a non-ledger example, e.g. 'a pure internal refactor with no surfaced API change'), never the surrounding mechanics. Run test_no_op_propose.py and the no-op assertions in test_pipeline_prompts.py after any edit. The planner should scope the no-op-block reword as part of work stream 1 (not the corpus sweep) so it lands with the other prompt edits under one reviewer.

risks.title: Documenter gateway boundary blocks code-docstring cleanup -> role-routing impasse
risks.description: Work stream 2 explicitly includes 'code docstrings/comments' (e.g. gateway/artifact_api.py:1, orchestrator/kubernetes_spawner.py with 30+ '# #3064 slice-N:' markers, shared/egg_anchor/protected_root.py:1). But DOCUMENTER_ROLE.blocked_write blocks **/*.py (and .ts/.go/.java...). The documenter CANNOT edit docstrings/inline comments inside source files — only docs/ and **/*.md. If the planner assigns docstring/comment cleanup tasks to the documenter role, the gateway push will be rejected and the slice will dead-end in an impasse. This is the single most likely concrete failure mode of the plan.
risks.mitigation: The planner MUST split work stream 2 by FILE TYPE as well as area: (a) pure-markdown targets (docs/, **/README.md, **/CLAUDE.md, **/*.md) -> documenter; (b) docstring/inline-comment targets inside *.py / source files -> coder. Do not route any *.py docstring task to the documenter. Reviewers should check each slice's task.role against the file extensions it touches before ACK. (This boundary is a hard constraint the issue says to PRESERVE — do not 'fix' it by widening documenter write access.)

risks.title: Corpus scope creep / merge churn vs HITL-bounded sweep
risks.description: 263 files carry ledger refs. cq-1 resolved to opt-1: enumerated named targets + bounded sweep of highest-density files, with the long tail explicitly deferred to follow-ups. Risk: (a) slices that sweep too broadly create large diffs that collide and rot against concurrent main activity (the repo is actively churning — see recent doc-updater commits); (b) an unbounded sweep silently turns into opt-2 (exhaustive) which the operator declined; (c) 'partial cleanup' is mistaken for 'complete' with no record of what was deferred.
risks.mitigation: Planner must (1) enumerate the EXACT target files per slice (the issue's named pages: docs/architecture/brc-memory.md, orchestrator.md, slice-dag.md, gateway-auto-filter.md, coordination-state.md, plus gateway/orchestrator/shared CLAUDE.md seam tables and the named docstrings) and a NAMED, COUNTED density-ranked sweep set; (2) slice by doc-area/package so slices don't collide on the same files; (3) emit an explicit 'deferred long tail' list (candidate follow-up issue) so completeness is auditable, not silent. Keep per-slice diffs reviewable.

risks.title: Over-deletion of load-bearing rationale (chronology vs rationale)
risks.description: The issue's sharpest boundary: 'not delete all issue references' — issue links and history that justify WHY the current system is shaped this way must stay (reframed as rationale). Several named pages are load-bearing: gateway-auto-filter.md has a 'what was removed / preserved for context' section; coordination-state.md encodes the '#3077 invariant ... final shape' with Threat/Mitigation tables. A mechanical strip of every 'slice-N / #NNNN / used to / now' token would destroy genuine design rationale and degrade the docs it is meant to improve. This is a correctness risk for the deliverable, not just churn.
risks.mitigation: Per-edit discipline: strip CHRONOLOGY (slice-N narration, 'landed in six slices', phase/HITL iteration numbers, change-log entries) but KEEP RATIONALE (why the design exists), reframed to present tense and isolated into a clearly-marked rationale note where substantial. Flag load-bearing pages (gateway-auto-filter 'what was removed', coordination-state '#3077 invariant') for TOTAL REFACTOR into current-state prose, not line-edits — the planner should name these explicitly. Reviewer_plan/reviewer_contract must verify each rewritten page still answers 'why is it built this way' where it did before. When in doubt, keep the rationale and drop only the dated framing.

risks.title: Self-referential ledger leak from this pipeline's own slices
risks.description: The cleanup's own work is sliced; agents could leave 'slice-N'/'#3288' ledger references in the very docs they are cleaning (e.g. 'cleaned in slice-2'), reintroducing the anti-pattern. Docs must be snapshots; the pipeline's process context belongs in commit messages/PRs, not in durable docs.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance check: grep the touched files post-edit for slice-N/TASK-N/this-pipeline references and confirm none were introduced. Documenter/coder must put process context only in commit messages.

risks.title: Re-drift after cleanup (no automated guardrail per cq-2)
risks.description: cq-2 resolved to NOT add a lint/CI guard this round (separable, own tuning cost). Consequence: the only durable mechanism preventing the corpus from re-accumulating ledger prose is the strength of the work-stream-1 documenter prompt revision. A weak/vague prompt edit means drift returns over time and the corpus pass amortizes poorly.
risks.mitigation: Make the work-stream-1 revision EXPLICIT and TESTABLE: concrete imperative instructions (write current-state snapshots; never emit slice/TASK/phase/HITL ids in docs/docstrings/comments; fold new state in and DELETE stale ledger lines rather than append; include history only as rationale). Add a unit assertion that the new instruction text is present (R1 mitigation) so it is regression-guarded. Record 'automated guardrail' as a noted candidate follow-up (operator-approved deferral), not a silent gap.

sequencing_recommendation: Land work stream 1 first (or in an early standalone slice): it is small (two files, text-only), establishes the snapshot standard the corpus pass then follows, and carries the no-op-block reword (R2) under one reviewer. Then slice work stream 2 by area AND file-type (markdown->documenter, code-docstrings->coder; R5), named-targets-first then a bounded density sweep with an explicit deferred list (R3).
acceptance_signals_for_reviewers: test_pipeline_prompts.py and test_no_op_propose.py green after work-stream-1 edits (R1, R2).
No documenter-role task targets a non-markdown source file; every *.py docstring/comment task is routed to coder (R5).
Each rewritten load-bearing page (gateway-auto-filter, coordination-state, *CLAUDE.md seam tables) still conveys design rationale, with chronology removed (R4).
Touched files contain no newly-introduced slice-N/TASK-N/#3288 ledger references (R6).
An explicit deferred-long-tail list exists so cq-1's bounded scope is auditable (R3).
Documenter gateway boundaries (allowed_write/blocked_write) and the BRC no-op propose path are unchanged in behavior (issue hard constraints).
